title: Information geometric quantification of effective privacy in quantum metrology
summary: Privacy of a quantum metrological protocol concerns the extent to which single parameters can be kept inaccessible to an observer or to other users of the network. In this work, an information geometric framework is developed to quantify privacy and accessibility of functions of parameters effectively, that is, up to a finite accuracy in state discrimination. Both quantities are defined by measuring volumes in the parameter space induced by the underlying quantum states.
